rules.message: uses the legacy queue concurrency limit (queue: { concurrencyLimit } or queues.overrideConcurrencyLimit / resetConcurrencyLimit); the concurrency option and concurrencyLimits replace them
rules.fix: use concurrency: { total, perKey } on the task, or a named concurrencyLimit() shared across tasks; manage it with concurrencyLimits.override / reset

rules.message: trigger options pass a queue object with name and concurrencyLimit; in SDK 4 a queue is declared ahead of time and only referenced by name at trigger time
rules.fix: declare const q = queue({ name, concurrencyLimit }) once, set it on the task (queue: q), and trigger with { queue: "name" }

rules.message: trigger options name a queue that no task in the project declares with queue({ name }); runs on it stay in Pending version until a deployed task declares it
rules.fix: declare const q = queue({ name }) and set it on a task (queue: q), or trigger with the name of a queue that is declared

rules.message: concurrency sets perKey without total; each key gets its own cap, but the total across all keys is unbounded
rules.fix: add total to the same concurrency object to bound all runs together

rules.judge: Look for a task whose run fans out to a rate-limited third-party API (LLM, email, payments, scraping) through batchTrigger / batchTriggerAndWait, a loop or map of .trigger() calls, or triggerAndWait inside a loop. Answer yes only if no cap bounds the parallel calls: no concurrency option on the task, no queue() with concurrencyLimit, and no concurrencyLimit() shared by the task. Answer no for internal work (database, in-process) and when a cap exists. Report the file and line of the fan-out.
rules.message: fans out calls to a rate-limited API, and no concurrency cap on the task or its queue bounds the parallel calls
rules.fix: add concurrency: { total: N } to the task, or share a concurrencyLimit({ name, total }) across the tasks that call the API

rules.message: queue name starts with "limit/" (reserved for concurrency limits, rejected at deploy time) or is longer than 128 characters
rules.fix: rename the queue: drop the "limit/" prefix and keep the name at 128 characters or fewer
